How do you fit 3D Garments in CLO?

To check fit, create and drape 3D Garments first. Draft your own Patterns in CLO or import Patterns created in other 2D CAD software to CLO, and then sew and drape Patterns on an Avatar. For more accurate fitting process, please use the Attach to Avatar Tape function to align the 3D Garment's shoulder seams to the Avatar's shoulder line. Then, select the desired texture rendering style from Transparent Surface, Fit Map, Stress Map, and Strain Map, and use various types of Garment Measure to further examine the fit.

Please use Chrome instead of other internet browsers. CLO website is optimized as Chrome. [CASE 1] If you didn't receive the verification email, please check your spam mailbox. What has changed in the Colorway Editor in CLO 7.3?

In CLO 7.3, creating colorways has become more diverse and easier compared to previous versions. You can now create colorways with increased variety, similar to actual colorways. The specific changes include: The number of each item can increase as much as the number of colorways, and by default, only the selected items are displayed in the Object Browser. ℹNote: Check out the entire colorway workflow in the manual or on YouTube. 1 Create more colorways by adding various items with different properties such as texture, buttons, topstitching, etc. In previous versions, adding items with different properties was not possible, limited to changing textures and colors only. However, starting from CLO 7.3, properties like texture, types, and sizes of buttons can be edited. 2 Manage identical items across different colorways When using certain items with the same properties across multiple colorways, you can now change all properties across those colorways by modifying just one item. 3 When applying each item (Fabric, Graphics, Buttons, Buttonholes, Topstitching, Puckering, Accessories) to a pattern, you can choose how they will be applied to the colorway. * Latest Updated on February 22, 2024, ver 7.3.240.46861 See the examples below and make your own selections as needed. You can learn how to apply each item here. A. Assign to the current colorway only This option is used when you want to apply different variations to selected colorway only. B. Assign to all colorways by linking color chips to change simultaneously Apply to all colorways, but if the fabric is the same for each colorway, selecting a color chip will automatically select the same fabric across colorways. C. Assign to all colorways by unlinking color chips so they change separately Apply to all colorways, but each colorway is a different fabric. FAQ Q1. When I add a different item to existing colorways, I cannot seem to edit them individually. How can I solve this problem? When adding a different item to existing colorways, they will be added with the same properties. If you wish to change properties in individual colorways, right-click on the color chip, then select 'Unlink All Colorways' to make individual edits. Q2. When I save a colorway file from the updated version and open it in a lower version, the colorway information disappears. How can I solve this issue? The new colorway format is not compatible with lower versions. As the colorway feature will be updated continuously, we recommend using the latest version. Q3. The Colorway Editor seems to be slower than in previous versions. Why is that? Each colorway consists of different items, which requires more time to update. However, we are continuously working on improving the speed issue, and incremental improvements will be made.

How can I express embroidery in CLO?

There are three possible ways to express embroidery in CLO differ by the purpose and the situation. With Scanned Embroidery Without Scanned Embroidery With Scanned Embroidery When there is a scanned image of embroidery, use the Graphic tools in CLO to express embroidery. However, as expressing thick embroidery and flat embroidery methods are different, please refer to the appropriate guide below. Express Embroidery with Thickness To express embroidery with thickness, please refer to below instruction. Create a rectangle Pattern in the 2D window. Apply a new fabric to the Pattern and add texture. Create Internal Lines in the shape of embroidery on the Pattern and cut. Delete unnecessary Pattern and duplicate the Pattern outline as an Internal Shape to the 3D Garment Pattern. Sew the embroidery Pattern to the 3D Garment. Click on the fabric item applied to the embroidery Pattern in the Object Browser and change its Preset as Fusible Rigid. Also, change the Particle Distance to 5. Express Flat Embroidery Use the Graphic tools to add the embroidery image to the 3D Garment in order to express embroidery with no thickness. Without Scanned Embroidery If there is no scanned image of embroidery, use the image editing tool such as Adobe Photoshop to express embroidery effects. Then, refer to guides from the With Scanned Embroidery section. You may search how to express embroidery in image editing tools online or take a look at the reference we found below! Video Link

Upon cancellation of your subscription, you will receive a confirmation email from CLO. If you did not receive a cancellation confirmation email within 24 hours, it is your responsibility to promptly contact CLO to receive written confirmation otherwise your cancellation request will be considered invalid. What does each mode represent?

Simulation Mode: Create and edit patterns in the 2D Window, working on garments, changing avatar poses, etc. in the 3D Window. Animation Mode: Record, play and edit garment animations. Print Layout Mode: Manually order patterns on prints to match texture placements in the 3D Window and calculate fabric consumption. Emulator Mode: Create physical properties for fabrics after measuring them out with the CLO Fabric Kit hardware. Modular Mode: Mix and match garment components such as sleeves and collars into blocks in order to evaluate and create new styles. Note: Found in the dropdown menu up to version 7.3 version 2024 and later features access to the Modular Library on the far left column of the software interface. UV Editor: Create UV maps of patterns, buttons, and zippers.

Why am I unable to log in to Help Center on iOS devices (or in the Safari app)?

Q: Why am I unable to log in to Help Center on iOS devices? A: Sometimes users encounter login issues when accessing the Help Center on their iOS device or using Safari. These issues are caused by the "Prevent cross-site tracking" setting, which blocks certain login data from being saved during the redirection process. This setting needs to be disabled in order for users to log in using Safari because the login process relies on cross-site tracking. By default, this setting is turned on, but users can manually disable it to resolve the issue. Apple's Help Center provides instructions on how to disable this setting, which can be found in the articles "Prevent cross-site tracking in Safari on Mac" or "Browse privately in Safari on iPhone".

What is the difference between CLO and Marvelous Designer?

Although the core technology behind the solutions are the same, Marvelous Designer is primarily used in the CG, animation, and gaming industries. CLO is a more robust solution geared towards the fashion and apparel industries with functions that can be applied to various stages of the garment design development process. The primary difference between the two solutions is that the import/export of DXF-AAMA or DXF-ASTM files in CLO, allows for production-ready patterns to be sent to your manufacturer.

CLO runs very slowly when I edit 3D Garment with Particle Distance 5. What should I do?

For all 3D garment simulation programs, its simulation speed varies depending on the number of meshes in a single file. More meshes there are, slower the speed is. On the other hand, less meshes there are, faster the speed is. When Patterns' Particle Distance is set to 5, the program naturally slows down due to increase of the number of meshes in a single file. Therefore, we STRONGLY insist you to increase the Particle Distance to 20 when editing 3D Garments and decrease it to 5 when the 3D Garment is fully completed. Then, simulate for about 1~2 minutes. Does CLO still run slowly though Patterns' Particle Distance is set to 20? This may happen when a Pattern is huge (e.g. flare skirt patterns,) because regardless of the Particle Distance value, bigger Patterns contain more meshes. Also, due to difference in their intrinsic character, the program speed may reduce when Patterns' mesh structure is set to Quadrangular. Please refer to Quadrangular/Triangular Mesh manual and configure mesh type as Quadrangular ONLY when needed. Moreover, program speed is also influenced by hardware specification. Please check out suggested specification here.

How can I export FBX from CLO to APEXFiz?

[Extract Patterns] is a function that is only supported by the 3D OPTION of APEXFIz. Below is a menu of CLO software. Select necessary avatar and patterns. Select multiple object, not single object. Export without combining vertex Select [Thin] for thickness. Select default [mm] for scale. If textures are required, select embed media.
